## Introduction

The fellowship is organised as a set of learning modules.

Each module focuses on one practical area of public health data work. Some modules are relevant to everyone. Others are more specialised.

The modules together form a flexible **learning library** that can support different roles across the health system.

---

## Responsible Data Practice

::: {.callout-note title="Module 1 – Responsible Handling of Health Data" collapse="false"}

Learn how to work safely and responsibly with confidential health data.

Topics include confidentiality, anonymisation, data minimisation, role-based access, and practical rules for working with small-population health data.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 2 – Responsible AI-Assisted Data Practice" collapse="true"}

Learn how to use AI tools safely in analytical work.

The module covers safe prompting, verifying AI outputs, avoiding hallucinated results, and keeping a transparent record of AI-assisted analysis.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 3 – Scientific Integrity and Analytical Transparency" collapse="true"}

Understand why honest and transparent analysis matters.

Topics include responsible interpretation, reproducibility, and avoiding misleading statistical claims.


:::

---

## Data Systems and Data Quality

::: {.callout-note title="Module 4 – Designing Health Data Systems" collapse="true"}

Learn the practical building blocks of health data systems.

Topics include identifiers, metadata, data dictionaries, and how datasets are structured so they can be used reliably.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 5 – From Raw Data to Analytical Dataset" collapse="true"}

Learn how to turn messy raw data into a clean analytical dataset using reproducible workflows.

Topics include data cleaning, documentation, and structured analytical pipelines.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 6 – Understanding Measurement and Survey Data" collapse="true"}

Learn how survey data are generated and where errors can arise.

Topics include measurement error, response bias, and interpreting survey-based indicators.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 7 – Data Quality in Surveillance Systems" collapse="true"}

Learn how to review the quality of surveillance or registry datasets.

Topics include missing data, duplicate records, completeness checks, and internal consistency.

:::

---

## Epidemiological and Statistical Analysis

::: {.callout-note title="Module 8 – Exploring Data and Understanding Variation" collapse="true"}

Learn how to describe data clearly using summary statistics and simple visualisations.

Topics include distributions, histograms, boxplots, and identifying unusual observations.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 9 – Disease Frequency and Health Indicators" collapse="true"}

Learn how to calculate and interpret the basic measures used in public health.

Topics include counts, proportions, rates, prevalence, incidence, and denominators.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 10 – Probability and Statistical Uncertainty" collapse="true"}

Learn the basic statistical ideas behind uncertainty in public health data.

Topics include probability, variability, and interpreting uncertainty in results.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 11 – Study Design in Epidemiology" collapse="true"}

Learn the main types of epidemiological study and what they can tell us.

Topics include cross-sectional studies, cohort studies, case-control studies, and sources of bias.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 12 – Confounding and Causal Thinking" collapse="true"}

Learn why statistical associations can be misleading.

Topics include confounding, causal reasoning, Simpson’s paradox, and careful interpretation of regression models.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 13 – Population Comparisons and Standardisation" collapse="true"}

Learn how to compare populations fairly.

Topics include age-specific rates, age standardisation, and why crude comparisons can be misleading.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 14 – Time-to-Event Analysis" collapse="true"}

Learn how to analyse outcomes that occur over time.

Topics include follow-up time, censoring, Kaplan-Meier curves, and interpretation of time-to-event results.

:::

---

## Communication and Public Health Intelligence

::: {.callout-note title="Module 15 – Data Visualisation and Communicating Risk" collapse="true"}

Learn how to present data clearly and honestly using simple graphics.

Topics include effective charts and avoiding misleading visualisations.

:::

::: {.callout-note title="Module 16 – Communicating Evidence for Policy and Practice" collapse="true"}

Learn how to turn analysis into useful public health intelligence.

Topics include technical notes, briefing papers, and short analytical summaries for decision-makers.

:::

---

## Using the modules

Some learners will complete only a few modules. Others may work through most of the sequence.

The modules are designed to support **gradual development of public health data capability within St Helena**.
